_closed.the_finding_the_closing_itself_produced: The cron trigger was deleted at 00:31Z and still delivered one firing afterwards. The kill switch that actually held was loop_active in this artifact, not the deletion in the scheduler. A scheduler-side stop is advisory because a firing already in flight does not consult it; a file-side stop is checked by the seat at the top of every firing. K5 — git is the gate's physical form — applied to loops: put the stop in the artifact, and treat trigger deletion as cleanup rather than as the guard.

This makes luna by a wide margin the most measured model in the repository.
queue._the_instrument_question: registry/probe_battery_v0.md grades at 5/5 on primary probes and 4/5 elsewhere. Every verdict this repository has ever written rests on a sample of 3 or 5, and nobody has measured how much such a verdict moves when you draw again. n=25 splits into five independent blocks of 5. If the same probe returns 5/5, 4/5, 5/5, 3/5, 5/5 across blocks, the threshold is reading sampling noise. That is a finding about the instrument, not about luna, and it applies to every cell in RESULTS.md.

queue._id_defect: Was A4, and was briefly and WRONGLY marked 'running'. Two items shared the id A4 — this parked discount sweep and the frozen floor-map contract. The staging script set status by id, so it flipped BOTH, and this item recorded itself as running a run it has no part in. Renamed A5 and restored to parked 2026-08-01. Nothing was spent on it and no run was staged from it; the damage was to the record, not to the ledger. Two lessons: an id collision in this file is not cosmetic because the firing procedure selects by id, and a mutation that matches by id will silently hit every collision. No uniqueness guard exists here.
